notes: Trade is the ferro-alloys of HS 7202 other than ferro-nickel, customs gross weight, by alloy, 15.8 Mt of exports in 2024 in all. The page opens on ferro-chromium, the largest alloy, and its key figure is that alloy's; ferro-manganese, silico-manganese, ferro-silicon and the other ferro-alloys together follow as tables of their own. The tables are not added to each other in any total of the page, and the figures are the weight of the alloy, not of the metal it holds.
Ferro-chromium (HS 720241, 720249), 2024 (CEPII BACI): world 7.61 Mt gross weight; top exporters South Africa 4.08 Mt, Kazakhstan 1.61 Mt, India 0.56 Mt.
Ferro-manganese (HS 720211, 720219), 2024 (CEPII BACI): world 1.74 Mt gross weight; top exporters India 0.69 Mt, Norway 0.35 Mt, Malaysia 0.23 Mt.
Ferro-silico-manganese (HS 720230), 2024 (CEPII BACI): world 3.28 Mt gross weight; top exporters India 1.11 Mt, Malaysia 0.40 Mt, Norway 0.32 Mt.
Ferro-silicon (HS 720221, 720229), 2024 (CEPII BACI): world 2.46 Mt gross weight; top exporters China 0.46 Mt, Norway 0.25 Mt, Malaysia 0.24 Mt.

The other ferro-alloys of heading 7202: ferro-silico-chromium, ferro-molybdenum, ferro-tungsten and ferro-silico-tungsten, ferro-titanium and ferro-silico-titanium, ferro-vanadium, ferro-niobium and the ferro-alloys not elsewhere specified (HS 720250, 720270, 720280, 720291, 720292, 720293, 720299), 2024 (CEPII BACI): world 0.69 Mt gross weight; top exporters China 0.17 Mt, Brazil 0.16 Mt, South Korea 0.03 Mt.
Ferro-nickel and nickel pig iron (HS 720260) are on the nickel page, where their group already was: no tonne is counted twice. The steel page leaves out HS 7201 to 7205.

No production table: USGS has no world table of the ferro-alloys. Price: the World Bank Pink Sheet has none for them. The only price on the page is the USGS annual average of ferro-chromium, per pound of chromium content, and of 75% ferrosilicon, in US cents per pound of silicon (United States salient statistics); no price series for the other alloys was loaded.

Ferro-manganese (HS 720211, 720219): the tables hold 1.74 Mt, 96% of the 1.82 Mt that the customs file records for these codes in 2024 (gross weight). The difference: 0.0765 Mt are pairs under the threshold of the extract (1,000 t and USD 1 million; 173 of the 912 pairs of the file are kept).

Ferro-silicon (HS 720221, 720229): the tables hold 2.46 Mt, 95% of the 2.59 Mt that the customs file records for these codes in 2024 (gross weight). The difference: 0.121 Mt are pairs under the threshold of the extract (1,000 t and USD 1 million; 338 of the 1,351 pairs of the file are kept).

The other ferro-alloys of heading 7202: ferro-silico-chromium, ferro-molybdenum, ferro-tungsten and ferro-silico-tungsten, ferro-titanium and ferro-silico-titanium, ferro-vanadium, ferro-niobium and the ferro-alloys not elsewhere specified (HS 720250, 720270, 720280, 720291, 720292, 720293, 720299): the tables hold 0.693 Mt, 94% of the 0.736 Mt that the customs file records for these codes in 2024 (gross weight). The difference: 0.0404 Mt are pairs under the threshold of the extract (1,000 t and USD 1 million; 483 of the 1,507 pairs of the file are kept).

Mozambique is among the importers of ferro-chromium (HS 720241, 720249) although it has no production line in the tables of this page and exports of 21 kt (0.27% of the world exports, 1.8% of its own imports), and the customs data record most of its imports as arriving overland: these tonnes may be cargo in transit to a port, and not the country's own use (a possible reading, not established here): the alloy comes overland from South Africa, the first producer of chromium ore in the USGS table of the Chromium page, and Mozambique has no line in that table.
